---
title: "Methodology & limitations"
description: "Sources, timing rules, uncertainty, and the boundary between descriptive football analysis and validated forecasts."
---

## Sources and publication boundary

The research uses nflverse play-by-play, participation data, and schedules
accessed through nflreadr and cached by the project. Closing spreads and
moneylines come from the cached schedules. The site's direct numerical inputs
are the nine saved `36_*` and `38_*` parquet artifacts listed in the
[provenance index](artifacts.qmd). This render does not fetch data or call a
pipeline loader.

The reviewed development and efficiency universe is NFL regular seasons
2021–2025. Strategy evaluation is 2022–2025, and saved model test predictions
cover 2024–2025. These are **season labels**, not exact calendar dates; the
selected parquet summaries do not preserve an exact game-date range or a
verified artifact-creation timestamp/SHA.

## No-lookahead rules

| Component | Timing rule and interpretation |
|---|---|
| Schematic win model (`R/36_win_probability_model.R`) | Trailing five-game team means followed by a one-game lag, reset each season. At least three prior games required; home-minus-away differences give one row per game. |
| Model split A | Fit 2021–2022; Platt calibration 2023; report 2024–2025. |
| Model split B | Fit 2021–2023; Platt calibration 2024; report 2025. |
| XGBoost early stopping | Internal temporal slice of training data; calibration data reserved for Platt scaling. |
| Power-index backtest (`R/38_market_backtest.R`) | Producer rebuilds the index with `lag_scores = TRUE`; mappings for season S use seasons strictly before S. The initial season is never bet. |
| Closing line | Unaltered evaluation benchmark; also the price/line against which strategy disagreement is measured. Not evidence of an earlier tradable opportunity. |

The stored descriptive power rankings are **not** safe same-game prediction
features. Likewise, the season-level matchup explainer and Markdown exporter
(`R/24_matchup_explainer.R`, `R/26_export_matchup_report.R`) provide structural
comparisons, not validated probabilities of a particular game outcome. Their
season aggregates can include information later than a named historical week.
The published PHI–DAL walkthrough is therefore labelled as a retrospective
engineering demonstration, not a pre-kickoff forecast. Its publication helper
disables market context and records the exact processed checkpoints it reads.

## Population and measurement choices

- The win-model EPA baseline uses regular-season run/pass plays, excluding
  penalties, kneels, and two-point attempts. Tied games are excluded from its
  binary win model. Do not generalise that population to every project table:
  broader descriptive metrics may include postseason plays.
- The power index is a hand-weighted composite. Its tiers are constructed
  editorial categories, not external labels learned from Bootleg Football.
- Four-man pressure is a proxy, not charted disguise. Coverage disguise is
  unavailable without external data. Personnel and pass-rusher counts depend
  on the participation join; absence is not a zero.
- In the closing-line convention, a positive spread denotes the home team's
  expected margin. Residual error is actual home margin minus closing spread.
- Efficiency regressions include the initial development season. They use
  ordinary regression standard errors. Failure to reject is not proof of no
  effect or universal market efficiency.
- The spread backtest excludes pushes; the moneyline implementation treats a
  tie as `home_won = 0`, not as an explicit sportsbook refund. This is a known
  settlement limitation, not a claim about how a live book would grade it.
- The reported spread ROI assumes −110 for every recorded bet. Moneyline ROI
  uses offered prices and fractional sizing; neither is a live-execution study.
- Thresholds overlap, seasons are few, and repeated experimentation can favour
  apparently promising results. No multiple-testing correction or independent
  prospective validation is claimed.
- The Brier bootstrap pairs predictions by game, not by team/season block.
  Dependence across games is not explicitly modelled. The two test windows
  overlap. Neither interval establishes incremental schematic value.

## Invalid research is not a null result

Old historical opening lines were generated from closing lines plus random
noise. The dependent opening-line movement / CLV studies (`R/17`–`R/19`) are
invalid, not evidence of successful timing and not a valid null finding.
`R/11_scrape_opening_lines.R` is now disabled. No synthetic-era performance
figures, QB direction-match hit rates, watchlists, or derived advice are reused.

This site is the **public-safe replacement**, not a republication of
`outputs/notebooklm/*.md` or historic research documents. Those files remain
unchanged and are not copied into the site output.

## Reproducibility is bounded

The renderer validates required artifacts and checks summary ROI against the
saved bet ledger. It reconstructs charts and tables, not the upstream models.
Render timestamp, checkout SHA, source paths, artifact hashes, and current
publication-source hashes are recorded. A checkout SHA is **not** proof that it
produced an existing artifact; missing historical lineage remains missing.
